title: 3rd Stopping Place 3rd Truth The Comparison Of The Army Of 400 000 Nations

questions.question: In the passage, what is spring presented as a sign or example of?
questions.answer: It is presented as a worldly example of the gathering after resurrection and of being brought back to life.

questions.question: About how many examples of reviving the dead are said to appear in spring, and over what time period?
questions.answer: Around three hundred thousand examples appear within a few weeks.

questions.question: What four forms of renewal are mentioned in connection with a tree?
questions.answer: The tree itself, its leaves, its blossoms, and its fruits.

questions.question: After spring is shown again in a way that matches the earlier one, what kinds of things are given to each species?
questions.answer: Each species receives its food, means of protection, distinguishing outward form, duties and release from duties, and whatever equipment it needs.

questions.question: How are these gifts and arrangements carried out? Give two or three features named in the passage.
questions.answer: They are carried out with precision and order, at the right time, and without mistake, neglect, or confusion.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat this springtime ordering like an army?
questions.answer: Because many different species are managed together in a disciplined and organized way, as if they were many groups within one great force.

questions.question: What qualities of Allah are said to be shown through this yearly renewal?
questions.answer: His unity, His absolute oneness, His uniqueness, His limitless power, and His endless mercy.

questions.question: Besides power and mercy, what other aspects of divine rule are said to appear here?
questions.answer: Perfect lordship, sovereignty, and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the image of writing on the face of the earth suggest about spring?
questions.answer: It suggests that spring openly displays a clear message of divine unity across the earth for anyone willing to notice it.

questions.question: What is the main point of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The careful revival and provision seen every spring serves as strong evidence that one all-powerful and merciful Lord governs all things.

questions.question: What central event in spring is used as evidence in this passage?
questions.answer: The repeated bringing to life of countless living kinds after a period that resembles death.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention “a few weeks” instead of a long span of time?
questions.answer: To stress how quickly and easily this vast renewal takes place.

questions.question: In what way does the example of the tree strengthen the argument?
questions.answer: It shows resurrection-like renewal not only in one broad sense, but in several layers within a single living thing.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by saying spring is shown again like the one before it?
questions.answer: It implies continuity, consistency, and deliberate control rather than random change.

questions.question: What is meant by each species receiving suitable provision and equipment?
questions.answer: Each kind is given what fits its own nature and needs, not a careless or one-size-fits-all share.

questions.question: Which is emphasized more in the passage: disorderly abundance or measured care?
questions.answer: Measured care is emphasized.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that things arrive unexpectedly yet on time?
questions.answer: Their arrival does not come from the creatures’ own planning, but from a higher will that provides exactly when needed.

questions.question: How does the passage connect spring to belief in one Creator rather than many powers?
questions.answer: It presents one coordinated system covering all species, which points to a single source of command and action.

questions.question: Why is mercy mentioned along with power?
questions.answer: Because the passage is not only about bringing things into existence, but also about caring for them and supplying what they need.

questions.question: If a student had to summarize the reasoning in one sentence, what would be a strong summary?
questions.answer: The ordered revival and care of hundreds of thousands of life forms each spring shows the work of one wise, powerful, and merciful Lord.

questions.question: What season is the focus of the passage, and why is it important?
questions.answer: Spring is the focus because it displays widespread renewal of life that points to resurrection.

questions.question: What number of life forms is highlighted in the passage’s description of the great living host?
questions.answer: Four hundred thousand different species are highlighted.

questions.question: How many revival-like instances are said to be seen in one tree?
questions.answer: Four.

questions.question: What does the repeated return of spring reveal about the way the world is governed?
questions.answer: It reveals stable, intentional, and wise governance.

questions.question: Name three categories of things given to the species in spring.
questions.answer: Nourishment, means of defense, and needed tools.

questions.question: What does the passage say about mistakes, neglect, and confusion in this process?
questions.answer: It says the process is free from them.

questions.question: What is the significance of things being given at the proper time?
questions.answer: It shows exact timing and purposeful care.

questions.question: According to the passage, what truths are proved by this springtime administration?
questions.answer: It proves divine unity, singularity, uniqueness, and unlimited power joined with vast mercy.

questions.question: What does the expression about a divine pen most likely mean here?
questions.answer: It refers to spring as a visible record or inscription of divine decree and message across the earth.

questions.question: How does the passage move from observation to belief?
questions.answer: It starts with visible patterns in spring and then draws theological conclusions from their order, scale, and precision.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does spring resemble in relation to the life to come?
questions.answer: It resembles the great gathering after resurrection.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by describing many spring events as examples of raising the dead?
questions.answer: It suggests that reviving life after apparent death is already shown repeatedly before our eyes.

questions.question: Why are leaves, flowers, and fruits mentioned separately from the tree itself?
questions.answer: To show that renewal happens in multiple distinct ways even within one organism.

questions.question: What does it mean that every group receives what is appropriate to it?
questions.answer: It means each type of creature is cared for according to its own specific condition and role.

questions.question: What balance is kept in the springtime ordering described here?
questions.answer: Vast diversity is managed together while precision and harmony are preserved.

questions.question: Which is the better description of the process in the passage: accidental growth or deliberate administration? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: Deliberate administration, because the passage stresses order, timing, suitability, and freedom from error.

questions.question: What can a reader infer from the phrase that things come in unexpected ways?
questions.answer: A reader can infer that their source goes beyond the creatures’ visible control and ordinary expectation.

questions.question: How do unity and oneness differ in the argument of this passage?
questions.answer: Unity points to one governing order over all, while oneness points to that same Lord’s unique and unmatched rule.

questions.question: Why does the passage join sovereignty with wisdom?
questions.answer: It presents rule not as raw force alone, but as authority exercised with knowledge, purpose, and proper measure.

questions.question: What overall lesson should a serious student take from this passage?
questions.answer: The yearly renewal of life is meant to be read as a clear sign of Allah’s sole rule, perfect wisdom, great mercy, and power to resurrect.

questions.question: What large-scale phenomenon in spring is used as the main proof in this passage?
questions.answer: The rapid reappearance and organized care of vast numbers of living species.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens within only a few weeks?
questions.answer: Hundreds of thousands of instances of renewed life are brought forth.

questions.question: Why is the single tree example important even though the passage speaks about many species?
questions.answer: It gives a close-up case showing that resurrection-like renewal can be seen clearly even in one familiar living thing.

questions.question: What repeated pattern from year to year is emphasized?
questions.answer: Spring returns in a way that matches the earlier spring.

questions.question: What are “defensive weapons” and “distinctive garments” pointing to in simpler terms?
questions.answer: They point to the natural protections and outward forms given to each species.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the quality of this provision and arrangement?
questions.answer: It describes it as exact, orderly, timely, and free from defects.

questions.question: What conclusion about divine power is drawn from this scene?
questions.answer: The power behind it must be unlimited, since it manages immense variety without failure.

questions.question: What conclusion about divine mercy is drawn from the same scene?
questions.answer: The One who governs also cares for creatures by supplying what each one needs.

questions.question: Why does the passage describe spring as a proclamation on the earth?
questions.answer: Because spring publicly announces the truth of divine unity through visible signs spread across the world.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the observations in nature and the beliefs affirmed in the passage?
questions.answer: The observations are treated as signs that support and confirm belief in Allah’s oneness and perfect rule.

questions.question: In this passage, what does spring teach about life after death?
questions.answer: It teaches that renewed life after death-like stillness is not strange, since examples of it appear widely every spring.

questions.question: What is the significance of the number three hundred thousand in the passage?
questions.answer: It refers to the huge number of revival-like instances displayed in spring.

questions.question: How does the passage use the example of a tree to make the argument more concrete?
questions.answer: It points to four visible forms of renewal in the same tree so the reader can picture the idea clearly.

questions.question: What kinds of care are given to the species in the “army of glory”?
questions.answer: They are given fitting sustenance, protection, outward features, assignments, release from assignments, and necessary means.

questions.question: What does the phrase “without confusion or omission” add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that nothing is overlooked and everything is managed in a controlled way.

questions.question: Why is timing so important in the passage’s description of spring?
questions.answer: Because right timing shows intention and rule, not blind chance.

questions.question: What theological truths are said to be demonstrated by this springtime order?
questions.answer: Allah’s unity, unmatched uniqueness, endless power, and boundless mercy are demonstrated.

questions.question: What does “perfection of dominicality” most nearly refer to in this context?
questions.answer: It refers to flawless lordship and care over creation.

questions.question: How should the phrase about writing with Divine Determining be understood?
questions.answer: It means that what happens in spring is like a visible inscription of Allah’s decree and message in creation.

questions.question: What is the best overall interpretation of the passage?
questions.answer: The passage argues that the disciplined renewal and provisioning of life each spring is a direct sign of one sovereign, wise, powerful, and merciful Creator.
